cards.text: Friend, the prophet Isaiah is passing along a message from the LORD to His people, Israel, who He also calls Jacob. The LORD calls Himself their Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel. And the first place He brings up? Babylon.

cards.question: The LORD, Israel's Redeemer, says He will send to Babylon. Whose sake does He say He's doing it for?

cards.text: Now, the Chaldeans of Babylon have ships, and they rejoice in those ships. Proud like a guy who just washed his truck and parked it across TWO spaces.

cards.question: The LORD says He will bring the Chaldeans down as ___ in the ships they rejoice in.

cards.text: Then the LORD says who He is: "I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, and your King." Four titles in one breath. Me? I've got Papa, and a name carved in my handle.
Then another "Thus says the LORD." This time He's described by what He's done: He makes a way in the sea and a path through the surging waters.

cards.question: In that picture of the LORD making a way through the sea, what happens to the chariots, horses, armies and warriors He brings out?

answers.text: They lie down never to rise again
They cross the sea behind His people
They turn around and head back home

cards.text: Isaiah says they're extinguished, "snuffed out like a wick." Like the birthday candle I shared that junk drawer with. Used once. Then pfft.

cards.question: Right after reminding Israel of the way He made through the sea, the LORD tells them to keep calling the former things to mind.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD says, "Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it?" That's God going, LOOK UP, it's happening RIGHT NOW!

cards.question: Before, the LORD made a way in the sea. For the new thing, where does He say He will make a way?

cards.text: And streams in the desert too. The LORD says the wild animals will honor Him for it, the jackals and the ostriches. An ostrich saying thank you? Friend, I would pay GOOD money to see that.

cards.question: The LORD says He provides water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert to give drink to His ___ people.
The LORD says the people He formed for Himself will declare His praise.

cards.text: Then the tone flips. After all that talk about rivers in the desert, the LORD turns to Jacob, to Israel, with some hard words.

cards.question: What does the LORD say Jacob, His people Israel, has not done?
The LORD says Israel hasn't called on Him because they have grown ___ of Him.

cards.text: Weary of the One who just promised rivers in the DESERT. Then the LORD gets specific: no sheep for burnt offerings, no honoring Him with sacrifices, no sweet cane bought with their silver.

cards.question: The LORD says He has burdened Israel with offerings and wearied them with frankincense.

cards.text: So nobody's been weighed down by offerings. But somebody HAS been weighed down. And friend, it's not Israel.

cards.question: What does the LORD say Israel has burdened Him with?

cards.text: Sins and iniquities, piled up on the LORD. This is the part where I'd expect God to slam the drawer shut and walk away.

cards.question: Instead, what does the LORD say He does with Israel's transgressions?
The LORD says He will keep remembering Israel's sins.

cards.text: "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake and remembers your sins no more." Not shoved in the back of a drawer under the dust. GONE.

cards.question: Then the LORD gives Israel an invitation. What is it?

answers.text: To argue the matter with Him
To bring Him a new offering
To leave the land for good

cards.text: "State your case, so that you may be vindicated." Then the LORD looks back at Israel's history, and the record He brings up isn't pretty.

cards.question: The LORD says Israel's first father sinned and their spokesmen rebelled against Him.
So the LORD says He will devote Jacob to ___ and Israel to reproach.

cards.text: And the princes of the sanctuary? Disgraced. Heavy place to land, friend. But don't forget who said "I, yes I" just a few verses back.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "Thus says the LORD.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "snuffed out like a wick.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card runs four sentences: 'Friend, the prophet Isaiah…Jacob.' / 'The LORD calls Himself…' / 'And the first place He brings up?' / 'Babylon.' The limit for an opening card is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD will 'bring the Chaldeans down as ___'. The BSB says 'bring them all as fugitives'. Adding 'down' changes the text's wording and adds a sense of humbling. It also hints at the answer, because it rules out 'conquerors'.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD is 'described by what He's done'. The text describes Him in the present tense: 'who makes a way in the sea'. The text gives no past time, and the card adds one.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question says 'Right after reminding Israel of the way He made through the sea'. The text never calls verses 16-17 a reminder. It also never links them to the 'former things' in verse 18. The card settles a connection that the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says 'it's happening RIGHT NOW!' The text says 'I am about to do something new; even now it is coming.' This turns 'about to' and 'coming' into something already happening.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'Before, the LORD made a way in the sea. For the new thing…' This sets verse 16 up as the past 'former thing' and contrasts it with the new thing. The text doesn't state that link, and it doesn't use a past tense.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card cites only Isaiah 43:24. Its first sentence, 'So nobody's been weighed down by offerings', retells Isaiah 43:23 ('I have not burdened you with offerings'). The citation should be Isaiah 43:23-24.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card quotes verse 25 in full. Cards 9 and 10 have just covered that verse: He blots out transgressions and remembers sins no more. The card restates what is already known and doesn't move the passage forward.
The setup says 'the record He brings up isn't pretty'. That gives away the answer to the true or false on card 14, which asks whether Israel's first father sinned and the spokesmen rebelled.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card ends with 'But don't forget who said "I, yes I" just a few verses back'. This suggests that verse 25's forgiveness softens or answers verse 28's judgment. The text doesn't say how the two verses connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
